claim_boundaries: Public-source evidence supports demos and synthetic scenarios only.
Public-source evidence does not prove conversion lift, ROI, autonomous-send safety, or paid production readiness.
Exact pricing, DIY spring or cable repair, commercial high-value jobs, and unsupported tenant policy questions require human review.

public_knowledge_slices.summary: DFW garage door providers commonly advertise Dallas-Fort Worth metro or Fort Worth-area service. Demo replies may ask for city or ZIP and must avoid promising coverage for a future tenant until its service area is approved.

Many DFW providers advertise same-day, 24/7, after-hours, or emergency service. Demo scenarios may show urgent acknowledgement and qualification, but public ads do not prove response-time performance.
Common garage door repair categories include springs, cables, rollers, tracks, panels, openers, sensors, off-track doors, noisy doors, and hardware issues.
Public guides support broad pricing ranges and after-hours fee caveats. Demo replies must avoid exact final pricing and explain that diagnosis, parts, door weight, and provider policy affect price.
Public forms and FAQs show intake fields such as name, phone, ZIP/city, service type, date, and confirmation messages. Demo booking must still require explicit customer acceptance.
Public guides and manuals warn that broken springs and torsion spring work can be dangerous. Demo behavior must not provide DIY spring or cable repair instructions.

Commercial doors, roll-up doors, high-speed doors, warehouse dock doors, manual chain hoists, and automatic operators appear in public service scope. Demo leads involving these should route to commercial/high-value review.
